title: Our Target Market
subtitle: How to describe your customers and who you are trying to reach
description: Learn the words marketers use to describe customer groups — their age, income, lifestyle, and what they care about.
dialogueSubtitle: Riley explains Brightline's target market to Dana in a planning meeting

vocabulary.definition: A fact about a group of people, such as their age, gender, or income.
vocabulary.example: Our key demographic is professionals aged 25 to 45 who work in marketing or sales.

vocabulary.definition: A range of ages that people belong to. For example: 18-24 or 35-50.
vocabulary.example: Our main age group is 30 to 45 — they are experienced but still open to new tools.

vocabulary.definition: Whether someone is male, female, or another identity.
vocabulary.example: Our product is used equally by all genders — we do not target one more than another.

vocabulary.definition: The money a person earns from their job.
vocabulary.example: We target people with a mid-to-high income who have a budget for marketing tools.

vocabulary.definition: The way a person lives — what they do, what they buy, and what they care about.
vocabulary.example: Our customers have a busy lifestyle — they want tools that save them time.

vocabulary.definition: A description of a typical customer — who they are and what they need.
vocabulary.example: We create a customer profile so the whole team understands who we are talking to.

vocabulary.definition: Something a person likes or cares about.
vocabulary.example: Our target customers have an interest in marketing, technology, and business growth.

vocabulary.definition: The way a person acts or what they do — for example, how they shop or use the internet.
vocabulary.example: We look at customer behaviour to understand when and how they use our product.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Decide to focus your marketing on a specific group of people.
phrasalVerbs.example: We target marketing managers at small and medium-sized companies.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Be interesting or attractive to a group of people.
phrasalVerbs.example: Our product appeals to people who manage large amounts of data every day.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Make a large group smaller by choosing the most important part.
phrasalVerbs.example: We narrowed down our target market to companies with 10 to 100 employees.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Say that your message or product is right for a certain group.
phrasalVerbs.example: This campaign speaks to busy professionals who do not have time to manage five tools.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Match the description of your typical customer.
phrasalVerbs.example: Dana fits the profile of our ideal client — small agency, growth-focused, marketing-savvy.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Using something as the reason or starting point for a decision.
phrasalVerbs.example: We choose our channels based on the behaviour and interests of our target market.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Riley, how does Brightline describe its target market? I am curious to know more.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: We start with the [[demographic:a fact about a group of people, such as their age, gender, or income]]. Our main customer is a marketing manager or business owner — usually between 30 and 45.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: So your main [[age group:a range of ages that people belong to]] is 30 to 45?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes — they are experienced enough to have a budget, but still open to new tools and ideas. We also look at [[income:the money a person earns from their job]] — we target people with a mid-to-high income.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Do you focus on a specific [[gender:whether someone is male, female, or another identity]]?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: No — our product is used equally by all genders. We focus more on job role and [[lifestyle:the way a person lives — what they do, what they buy, and what they care about]]. Our customers are busy people who want to save time.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: What are their main [[interest:something a person likes or cares about]]s?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Marketing, technology, and business growth. We look at [[behaviour:the way a person acts — for example, how they shop or use the internet]] too — our best customers are the ones who check their data every day.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Do you have a customer [[profile:a description of a typical customer — who they are and what they need]]?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes — we call her 'Marketing Maya'. She is 35, runs a small team, loves data, and is always looking for a better way to manage campaigns.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Ha — that sounds a lot like me!

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: You fit the profile perfectly, Dana. That is exactly why I thought Brightline would be a great fit for your agency.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the question or comment. Talk about which response (A, B, or C) is best. Choose together, then click to check.

options: We target small and medium-sized businesses.
Our main target is marketing managers and business owners aged 30 to 45, with a mid-to-high income, who have a busy lifestyle and want to save time on their campaigns.
We work with anyone who is interested in our product.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives the job role, age group, income level, and the lifestyle reason — a complete, clear answer. A says too little. C sounds like you have no specific target, which is not good marketing.

items.customerLine: Do you target men or women?
options: Mainly men, because most marketing managers are men.
We do not focus on gender — our product is used equally by all genders. We focus more on job role, income, and lifestyle.
It depends on the campaign.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives a clear answer — gender is not the focus — and says what you do focus on instead. A makes an assumption that is not true. C avoids giving a real answer.

items.customerLine: How do you know who to target?
options: We look at who buys our product most often.
We build a customer profile based on demographics like age and income, but also on behaviour and interests. We then look at which customers get the most value from the product.
We target everyone and see who responds.
items.explanation: B is correct. It explains the method clearly — customer profile, demographics, behaviour, interests, and value. A is too simple. C sounds like there is no real targeting at all.

items.customerLine: What does your ideal customer look like?
options: We call her 'Marketing Maya'. She is 35, runs a small marketing team, loves data, and is always looking for a better way to manage campaigns.
Our ideal customer is a professional who is interested in marketing.
We have many types of ideal customer.
items.explanation: A is correct. It gives a specific, vivid profile — name, age, role, behaviour, and motivation. This is exactly how a good customer profile is described. B is too vague. C avoids giving a clear picture.

profileMatch.instructions: You are Riley. Look at three potential customers. As a group, decide which ones fit Brightline's target profile best. Use vocabulary from this lesson to explain your choices. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: Alex, 38 — Marketing Manager
profiles.description: Alex manages a team of four people at a tech company. He has a good income and checks his campaign data every morning. He uses three different marketing tools and finds it frustrating.

profiles.name: Priya, 22 — Marketing Assistant
profiles.description: Priya just started her first job in marketing. She is enthusiastic but does not have a budget to spend on tools. She uses free platforms and learns on the job.

profiles.name: Tom, 50 — Business Owner
profiles.description: Tom owns a small business but does not manage marketing himself. He has a good income but is not interested in technology tools. He prefers to work with agencies.

options.label: Fits the profile
options.description: This person matches the demographic, lifestyle, behaviour, and interests of Brightline's ideal customer. They have the budget and the motivation to use the product.

options.label: Not yet — wrong age group or income
options.description: This person is interested in marketing but does not have the income or the budget to buy a paid tool right now. They might be a good customer in the future.

options.label: Not the right fit
options.description: This person does not match the profile — they have a different lifestyle, they are not interested in marketing tools, or they prefer a different way of working. Not a good target for this product.

finishTheLine.instructions: The marketer's line is not finished. As a group, discuss how you would finish it. Use vocabulary from this lesson. There is no single correct answer — compare your ideas, then click to see one example.

items.customerLine: How would you describe your ideal customer?
items.salespersonStart: Our ideal customer is a marketing manager or business owner, aged 30 to 45. They have a busy lifestyle and a mid-to-high income.
items.suggestedCompletion: They are interested in technology and business growth, and they want to save time by managing everything in one place. We call this person 'Marketing Maya' — she is our customer profile.

items.customerLine: How do you decide which age group to target?
items.salespersonStart: We look at which age group gets the most value from our product. The 30-45 age group is our main focus because
items.suggestedCompletion: they have the experience to know what they need and the income to pay for a good tool. Younger customers often do not have the budget yet, and older customers may be less interested in new technology.

items.customerLine: Do you look at customer behaviour when planning a campaign?
items.salespersonStart: Yes — behaviour is one of the most important things we look at. We want to know when our customers use the product, how often they check their data, and
items.suggestedCompletion: what actions they take before they decide to buy. That behaviour tells us when and where to reach them with our marketing.

items.customerLine: Why is it important to have a customer profile?
items.salespersonStart: A customer profile helps the whole team understand who they are talking to. Without it,
items.suggestedCompletion: different people on the team will have different ideas about who the customer is — and the message will not be clear or consistent. A good profile helps everyone speak to the same person.
